name: Spinal and bulbar muscular atrophy (Kennedy disease)

clinicalPearls: An X-linked recessive lower motor neuron disorder affecting adult men, caused by an expanded CAG trinucleotide repeat in the androgen receptor gene (AR)
Presents in mid-adult life with slowly progressive proximal limb weakness, cramps, and prominent bulbar involvement including dysarthria, dysphagia and tongue atrophy
Perioral and chin fasciculations and a characteristic postural or action tremor are useful clinical clues
Partial androgen insensitivity produces gynaecomastia, testicular atrophy and reduced fertility
The disorder is a polyglutamine disease; longer CAG expansions tend to correlate with earlier onset
Sensory involvement is frequently detectable on nerve conduction studies even when clinically silent, reflecting a sensory neuronopathy component
It must be distinguished from amyotrophic lateral sclerosis, which it can mimic but from which it differs by its slower course, absence of upper motor neuron signs, and androgen features
reference.pathophysiology: Spinal and bulbar muscular atrophy is caused by an expanded CAG trinucleotide repeat encoding a polyglutamine tract in the androgen receptor. The expanded, ligand-activated receptor misfolds and accumulates, exerting a toxic gain of function that preferentially damages lower motor neurons in the brainstem and spinal cord, together with dorsal root ganglion sensory neurons. Because the toxicity is androgen-dependent, disease is largely confined to men, while the same receptor dysfunction produces partial androgen insensitivity with gynaecomastia and reduced fertility. Progressive motor neuron degeneration leads to bulbar and proximal limb weakness and muscle atrophy.
additionalDifferentials: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis / motor neuron disease
additionalInvestigations: Genetic testing for the androgen receptor CAG repeat expansion, which is diagnostic
Electromyography and nerve conduction studies showing chronic neurogenic changes with reduced sensory action potentials
Serum creatine kinase, often moderately elevated
Endocrine assessment including testosterone, gonadotrophins and lipids/glucose given metabolic associations
Swallowing assessment to quantify aspiration risk
Family history and genetic counselling regarding X-linked inheritance
redFlags: Significant dysphagia with aspiration and weight loss
Choking episodes or nocturnal respiratory symptoms
Rapid deterioration suggesting an alternative motor neuron disease
reference.prognosis: The condition progresses slowly over decades and life expectancy may be near normal or only modestly reduced, with morbidity and mortality driven mainly by bulbar dysfunction, aspiration and falls. Most affected men remain ambulant for many years before requiring aids.
pitfalls: Misdiagnosing the condition as amyotrophic lateral sclerosis and giving an inappropriately grave prognosis
Overlooking the androgen features (gynaecomastia, subfertility) that point to the diagnosis
Failing to recognise the subclinical sensory neuronopathy on nerve conduction studies
Not counselling about X-linked inheritance and carrier status in female relatives
references: Adams and Victor's Principles of Neurology
OMIM: Spinal and bulbar muscular atrophy (AR)
management: Provide supportive, symptom-directed care coordinated through a specialist neuromuscular clinic, as no disease-modifying therapy is established for the androgen-receptor CAG expansion
Maintain mobility and prevent contractures with physiotherapy, occupational therapy and appropriate aids, and treat dysarthria with speech and language therapy
Manage bulbar dysfunction with regular swallow assessment, diet-texture modification and consideration of gastrostomy feeding when aspiration risk is high
Monitor and treat the metabolic and endocrine complications of partial androgen insensitivity, including gynaecomastia, dyslipidaemia and impaired glucose tolerance
Surveil respiratory function and aspiration risk, treating chest infections promptly and instituting airway-clearance measures
Reduce falls through home assessment, mobility aids and provision of psychological support
Offer genetic counselling for X-linked recessive inheritance, with carrier testing for female relatives and reproductive counselling
